title: How Tibo shipped 10 failed products, then built Tweet Hunter and a $1M/month SaaS portfolio
summary: Tibo Louis-Lucas explains his revenue-first validation approach, shipping a product a week until one stuck, going deep on a single platform, and giving product-level equity to influencers for distribution. He also covers why he now avoids selling, uses DMs over calls, and runs five product-led SaaS solo with AI.

principles.text: Validation means paying customers, not free users or usage.
principles.quote: the number one mistake that most people do is thinking that having some usage of your product, having some free users is validation

principles.text: Ship a new product every week until one sticks, and never spend years on an unvalidated idea.
principles.quote: ship one new product every week until something stick.

principles.text: Beat saturated horizontal tools by going full depth on one platform for individuals.
principles.quote: we just integrated one social media, Twitter, but we went like full depth on on this one.

principles.text: Give a distribution partner a product-level share (profit and exit) so they are strongly incentivized to promote.
principles.quote: we gave away 25% of the product to a Twitter influencer who would be like the the head of distribution

principles.text: Treat promoters like investors, with no obligation to promote and regular financial updates; most still promote.
principles.quote: they were really not used to being treated as investors.

principles.text: Learn from DM conversations with early users rather than public launch announcements; avoid calls to protect focus.
principles.quote: it's more about like having a real conversation with people when they're trying your product.
